title_en: Working Rules of the Compensation Committee of the Supreme People's Court
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Working Rules of the Compensation Committee

Fa Fa [1999] No. 16

(Adopted at the 7th Meeting of the Compensation Committee of the Supreme People's Court on April 26, 1999)

Article 1. These Rules are formulated in accordance with the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China and relevant legal provisions, for the purpose of standardizing the work of the Compensation Committee and giving full play to its functions.

Article 2. Tasks of the Compensation Committee

(1) To discuss and decide the following cases:

1. State compensation cases in which a compensation claimant applies to this Court for compensation and the compensation decision should be made by this Court;

2. Cases in which a decision of the Compensation Committee of this Court is challenged and a new compensation decision needs to be made;

3. Cases in which a party files a petition with this Court against a decision of the Compensation Committee of a Higher People's Court and this Court decides to take the case for trial;

4. Cases involving major or difficult issues in the application of law referred by Higher People's Courts or the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army;

5. Other major or difficult cases.

(2) To discuss draft judicial interpretations.

(3) To discuss and study major matters in compensation work, summarize experience in compensation work, and supervise and guide the compensation work of courts at all levels in local areas.

(4) To discuss and decide other major matters related to compensation work.

Article 3. Matters to be discussed by the Compensation Committee shall be submitted by the Chairperson or the Vice Chairperson.

Article 4. The Compensation Committee shall hold a regular meeting once every two months, and may convene meetings at any time when necessary.

Article 5. For the topics to be discussed by the Compensation Committee, the Office of the Compensation Committee shall send the relevant documents and materials to each committee member and relevant non-voting participants one day prior to the meeting.

Upon receiving notice of the meeting, members of the Compensation Committee shall attend the meeting on time. Those who are unable to attend due to reasons shall inform the Office of the Compensation Committee one day in advance.

Article 6. Meetings of the Compensation Committee shall be presided over by the Chairperson, or by the Vice Chairperson as authorized by the Chairperson.

Article 7. Meetings of the Compensation Committee shall be held with the participation of more than half of the members.

The Compensation Committee practices democratic centralism. Decisions on cases discussed by the Compensation Committee must be approved by more than half of all members of the Committee. The opinions of the minority may be reserved and recorded in the file.

Article 8. Major and difficult cases discussed by the Compensation Committee, or cases with substantial disagreement, may be submitted to the Judicial Committee for discussion upon the decision of the Chairperson or Vice Chairperson presiding over the meeting.

Article 9. For cases or other matters discussed by the Compensation Committee, the case handler shall make preparations, report in accordance with the requirements of the person presiding over the meeting, and be responsible for answering questions raised by committee members.

Article 10. The Office of the Compensation Committee shall implement decisions of the Compensation Committee and shall not alter them without authorization; if new circumstances are discovered, it may request the Chairperson or Vice Chairperson of the Compensation Committee to decide whether to submit the matter to the Compensation Committee for further discussion.

Article 11. Meeting minutes shall be prepared for matters discussed and decided by the Compensation Committee. The minutes shall be reviewed and approved by the person presiding over the meeting, printed, and distributed to each committee member. They may also be distributed to the Compensation Committees of Higher People's Courts as needed. The Office of the Compensation Committee shall keep the meeting minutes on file for reference.

Article 12. The Office of the Compensation Committee is the specific working body of the Compensation Committee, responsible for case adjudication, drafting of judicial interpretation drafts, preparation before meetings of the Compensation Committee, meeting records, and drafting of meeting minutes. In accordance with the arrangements and requirements of the Compensation Committee, it shall specifically implement the supervision and guidance of compensation work in local courts at all levels, conduct research and investigations on the experience and existing problems of compensation work nationwide, summarize experience, and handle other specific matters related to compensation work.

Article 13. Members of the Compensation Committee and other participants attending the meeting shall comply with confidentiality provisions and shall not disclose the discussions of the Compensation Committee.

Article 14. These Rules shall come into force as of the date of adoption.

May 31, 1999
